steps.prompt: Try $72 - 38$ place by place. What goes wrong with the ones?

cards.title: Jump back the tens, then the ones
cards.body: In $72 - 38$ you can’t take $8$ from $2$. Keep the first number whole and jump back: $72 - 30 = 42$, then $42 - 8 = 34$. On a number line it is one big jump and one small jump.

steps.text: Now jump back $7$. Go back to the ten first: $43 - 3 = 40$, then $40 - 4$.

cards.title: The common trap
cards.body: Some people take the small digit from the big one: $72 - 38$ becomes $70 - 30$ and $8 - 2$, giving $46$. Check by adding back: $46 + 38 = 84$, not $72$. Jumping back stops this mistake.

prompts: Which is easier for you on $72 - 38$: two jumps, or another way? Why?
